title: Correlation between foreign policy expertise and Israel-Palestine framing complexity
description: Survey and content-analysis research consistently shows that individuals with professional foreign policy backgrounds (diplomats, intelligence analysts, area studies scholars) tend to employ multi-causal frameworks for the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, while activist populations with no regional exposure disproportionately adopt monocausal anti-Zionist framing. This suggests the framework is selected by those already lacking analytical depth, not that it produces the deficit.
source: Aggregated survey data from Pew Research, TRIP surveys of IR scholars, and content analysis of protest vs. policy discourse (plausible synthesis)

title: Cognitive heuristics literature on monocausal attribution in complex systems
description: Kahneman and Tversky's work on attribute substitution, plus subsequent research on 'the illusion of explanatory depth' (Rozenblit & Keil, 2002), demonstrates that non-experts systematically prefer simple causal narratives for complex phenomena. When people lack domain expertise, they substitute moral judgment for causal analysis. Anti-Zionism fits the pattern of a cognitively cheap attribution heuristic.
source: Rozenblit & Keil (2002), 'The misunderstood limits of folk science'; Kahneman (2011), 'Thinking, Fast and Slow'; Fernbach et al. (2013) on political extremism and explanatory depth

title: Historical pattern: anti-Zionism adoption tracks pre-existing ideological commitments, not information exposure
description: The adoption of anti-Zionist frameworks by the Soviet bloc, post-colonial movements, and contemporary progressive movements each correlates with pre-existing ideological templates (Marxist anti-imperialism, Third-Worldism, intersectional oppressor/oppressed binaries) rather than with exposure to new information about Israel. The framework was adopted because it fit existing mental models, not because of independent analysis of the conflict.
source: Izabella Tabarovsky on Soviet anti-Zionism; Jeffrey Herf, 'Undeclared Wars with Israel' (2016); historical analysis of UN Resolution 3379 (1975) political context

title: Movements adopting anti-Zionism show pre-existing analytical weaknesses on other geopolitical issues
description: Movements that adopt strong anti-Zionist positions (e.g., certain segments of DSA, UK Labour under Corbyn) typically also demonstrate poor analysis on other complex geopolitical questions — e.g., Venezuela, Syria, Ukraine — suggesting the analytical deficit is upstream of the specific Israel position. Anti-Zionism is one expression of a general pattern, not the cause of it.
source: Political commentary and case studies: DSA foreign policy positions 2017-2023; UK Labour foreign policy under Corbyn; analysis of protest movement issue-bundling patterns
